name: Farrier

pf.license.need: Usually none: most places license neither farriers nor horse shoeing. A farrier may hold a voluntary certification, which shows only as the business's own word. A city or county may ask for a business license. The state's or city's form says which.
pf.license.ask: The business registration or local business license number, where the form asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: The business. A certification, where a farrier has one, is that farrier's own word.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.insurance_bond: Liability insurance that covers horses in the farrier's care is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.
pf.license.not_this_work: Sedation, vet care, hoof surgery, horse training, boarding and teeth floating are other kinds of work, with their own plug-ins.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: a farrier comes to the customer's barn on a set day, usually every 6 to 8 weeks, and the owner or a handler holds the horse. A horse can also be trailered to the farrier's shop, where the owner stays with it.

pf.services.capacity: One farrier does about 6 horses a day. Up to 4 horses of one owner go on one booking; a bigger barn is booked as more visits. The shop works on 3 horses a day in two bays.
pf.services.nobody_home: No. The owner or an adult handler stays with the horse for the whole visit. A child alone never holds a horse.
pf.services.not_offered: Sedation or any vet care, horse training, boarding and teeth floating (other work). A horse that can't be caught or held safely isn't worked on until a handler is there or a vet has sedated it.

The vet's written plan for corrective or therapeutic shoeing
The horse's health conditions and medicines
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult (18 or older) who owns the horse or leases it with the owner's OK. A barn manager books for a boarder only with the owner's OK. Nobody under 18 books, and a teen holds a horse only with an adult at the barn.

words: a horse that is hurt, bleeding badly, down, in colic pain or can't put weight on a leg, right now
a person kicked, stepped on or bitten and hurt
a horse loose on a road or lost right now
a horse with hot, painful hooves that won't walk
a horse that can't be held safely
what_happens: A horse hurt, down, in colic pain or unable to bear weight now: Rosie can't judge how sick a horse is. It says to call the vet, or an emergency equine vet, now. No booking until the horse is safe.
A horse loose now: Rosie gives the business's number to call, and tells the owner at once.
Hot, painful hooves that won't walk: no trimming or shoeing until a vet has seen the horse. The vet's written plan then goes on the secure page.
A horse that can't be held safely: no work until a handler is there or a vet has sedated it. The farrier can stop at any time.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: No, for an emergency now or for hot, painful hooves. Yes, after the owner's OK, for a horse that has kicked or bitten. Yes with a handler or a vet's sedation, for a horse that can't be held.

pf.first_steps.hoof_check: No separate meeting. A new horse's first visit starts with a free 15-minute hoof check at the barn: the farrier looks at how the horse stands and at the hooves before any work.
pf.first_steps.forms: On the secure page, before the first visit: a handling release (the owner answers for how the horse is handled; horses can be unpredictable), an emergency contact, and a vet-care OK with a spending limit the customer sets (the example: up to $500).
pf.first_steps.plan: A 6-week plan gets its own yes after the first visit, and its terms are texted back. If the first check shows the horse needs a vet first, the plan waits and nothing is charged.
prep_for_reminder: Catch and clean the horse, and bring it to the work area
Have a handler there to hold the horse
Keep other horses and dogs away from the work area
Put the gate code on the secure page, never in a text

pf.visit.check_in: At the barn: the owner or handler gives the check-in code to the farrier at the work area. At the shop: the code is given at the shoeing bay. DONE with a photo of the finished hooves confirms the visit.
pf.visit.entry_codes: Gate or barn codes are shown only to the farrier on the job, on the visit day. Each use is logged. Deleted 72 hours after the plan ends.
pf.visit.handler: The owner or an adult handler stays with the horse for the whole visit. A child alone doesn't hold a horse. If nobody is there, the farrier waits 15 minutes, then leaves, and the owner decides any fee.
pf.visit.visit_report: The work done, the shoe sizes, hoof notes for next time, and a photo.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: Pads, a wall repair or an extra horse only when the customer says yes first, priced from the list. It is paid with the visit.
pf.visit.proof_done: DONE with the work done and a photo of the finished hooves.
pf.visit.weather: Lightning, heavy rain, ice or heat over the owner's limit: the work moves to a covered area or to another day, no fee.

pf.money.start: Barn calls: a card saved for the trip fee at booking, and the visit charged to it at DONE. Sam can send a bill after the visit instead, for barns that pay by link, or take nothing for a known barn. Corrective shoeing is priced after the farrier looks: only the trip fee is promised, the farrier quotes at the barn, the owner says yes, and the card is charged at DONE. At the shop: a card saved for the late-cancel fee, paid at the counter after. The hoof check for a new horse is free.
pf.money.deposits: None. Nothing is held for a visit.
pf.money.fees: A late cancel (the example: inside 24 hours) or a no-show: up to $50 at the barn and $20 at the shop, only if the owner confirms. No answer, no fee. With no handler, the farrier waits 15 minutes, then leaves; the owner decides any fee. A change the business makes never costs the customer.
pf.money.plans: Each plan visit is charged at its own DONE, or billed after by text. Rosfield's $2 counts once a month for a plan.
pf.money.tips: Optional, all to the farrier. A tip line only if the owner turns it on.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes farrier services, from the state form.
pf.money.rosfield_fee: The usual $2 per confirmed booking, once a month for a plan.

never_in_texts: A horse's health conditions, medicines and vet records
pf.messages.photos: Visit photos go only to the customer and the business. They show the hooves and the horse, never people or the barn's address. They are shown to others only with the customer's yes.
pf.messages.urgent: A person kicked, a horse loose or a horse hurt at a visit: the owner and the customer are told at once, at any hour. Rosie then steps back, and never admits fault or offers money.
pf.messages.minors: Nobody under 18 books. A teen at the barn isn't the booking's adult.

skills: Corrective and therapeutic shoeing (lead farrier only)
Hot shoeing and custom shoes at the forge
pf.staff.licenses: None per person unless the state's form says so. A certification is the farrier's own word.
pf.staff.new_person_ok: A farrier the customer hasn't met works only after the customer's OK by reply, or after the owner calls them. No answer: the owner calls first, or the visit is skipped with no charge.
pf.staff.ratio: One farrier at each horse. An apprentice works only while the lead farrier is on the job.
pf.staff.who_oks: The owner OKs a horse with a kicking history, every fee, every refund and every corrective shoeing price. The office manager may OK prices over the limit; the owner's answer wins.

plans: The plan's terms show before any card is asked: the day and window, the price a visit, when it's charged, skip and weather terms, that it runs until ended, and how to end it.
The plan gets its own yes, apart from the booking, and the terms are texted back.
A price change is told 30 days ahead, or more where the state's rules ask.
Once a year, the terms and how to end the plan are texted again (the business's own rule), plus any reminder the state's rules require.
pf.rules.agreement: A signed handling release and vet-care OK before the first visit (the business's own rule).
pf.rules.free_reset: A shoe that comes off within 7 days of a visit is reset free, with the owner's OK (the business's own rule).
pf.rules.local_rules: Trailer, barn and animal transport rules, as the state's form sets them.
pf.rules.records: 3 years, with the shoeing notes and anything that happened at a visit (the business's own rule).

matter_most: A horse kicks or hurts a person: help and 911 first; the owner and Sam are told at once. Rosie never admits fault or offers money.
A horse that can't be held: no work until a handler is there or a vet has sedated it; the owner decides any fee.
Hot, painful hooves found at a visit: the farrier stops, a vet comes first, and the owner gets a written note.
A shoe thrown within 7 days of a visit: a free re-set visit that Sam OKs.
A horse loose at the barn: the owner and Sam are told at once.
A farrier is out: someone the customer hasn't met works only after the customer's OK. No reply: the owner calls first, or a free skip.
Weather day: lightning, heavy rain, ice or heat moves the work to a covered area or another day, or a free skip.
Pads, a wall repair or an extra horse found at the visit: price and a yes first, paid with the visit.
Skip, pause or end a plan. A skip after the cutoff may be charged, only if the owner confirms.
An apprentice works only while the lead farrier is on the job.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
Built Tue Oct 27 2026 from the refitted groomer (from: groomer); the plug-in, rename pairs, money and every own step were rewritten for farrier work. A farrier is a barn-call trade (a horse is not left at the shop), so the groomer's drop-off steps are not used: the owner or a handler stays with the horse. No sample or test-drive plug-in existed, so it is built from the trade's norm and says so here.
Work: a farrier trims and shoes horses every 6 to 8 weeks. Flow B (the usual side) is Lee Mobile Farrier at Alex's barn, 6 Pasture Ln: a full set of shoes for Juniper, a quarter horse mare, Thu Oct 22, arriving 8 to 10am, with Tate and Alex holding her. Flow A (the less usual side) is Lee Forge Shop, Sam's second company: Alex trailers Dusty, a gelding, to the shop, 40 Anvil Rd, for a trim with Rowan, Sat Oct 24 at 11:00am, stays with Dusty in the bay and pays at the counter.
Prices (the example business's own): at the barn trim $65, full set of shoes $179, hoof pads $20 a hoof, therapeutic shoes from $199, reset a thrown shoe $45, trip fee (late cancel or no-show) up to $50; corrective shoeing is priced after the farrier looks. At the shop trim $35, trim with wall repair $40, pull shoes $20, foal trim $25, front shoes $55, full set $140, late-cancel fee $20, hoof evaluation $25 before corrective work. The hoof check for a new horse is free. A shoe thrown within 7 days of a visit is reset free, with Sam's OK.
Money paths. B: list|card|card (main: $179, card saved for the $50 trip fee, charged at DONE), list|card|bill (the same, Rosie texts the bill), list|none|bill (a $65 trim for a known barn, nothing taken), visit|card|card (corrective shoeing priced at the barn; only the $50 trip fee is promised; $245 in the quote example = $165 shoes + $80 pads, four hooves at $20). A: list|card|counter (main: $35 trim, card saved for the $20 fee, paid at the counter), list|none|counter (a horse the shop knows), visit|card|counter (corrective shoeing priced at the shop; only the $25 hoof evaluation is promised). No hold, no deposit, no full price: farriers are paid at the visit. Pads or an extra horse found at the visit need a yes and are paid with the visit.
